restatement: Fix the template resolver's condition evaluator, editing only nodes/TemplateResolver/expressions.ts, so conditions mean what they say. NOT a, !a and NOT (a) must negate. &&, ||, and case-insensitive and/or must work as AND/OR, with AND binding tighter. AND/OR inside quoted literals must not split a condition. An unquoted right-hand side of contains/startsWith/endsWith must be read as a variable. == and != must compare numerically when both sides are numeric, and a missing variable must equal null. An unknown word next to an operator must raise an error instead of quietly evaluating to false. The change must not alter other behavior, must not edit or delete existing tests, and must not add a runtime dependency. It serves the cycle goal of fixing the Tier 0 bugs in a deterministic, no-eval template language.
verification_plan: Confirm that the diff touches only nodes/TemplateResolver/expressions.ts, with no test edits or deletions and no package.json or dependency change (m2, m3, scope).
For each frozen regression test, trace the pre-fix code path and confirm it fails for the reason the criterion names, then trace the post-fix path and confirm it passes (c1-c6).
c1: NOT a, !a, NOT (a) and the existing NOT(a) all negate; != is not taken as negation.
c2: &&, ||, and/or in any case split correctly; OR is lowest precedence and AND binds tighter; not combines inside and/or.
c3: logical splitting skips single- and double-quoted spans; a real AND outside the quotes still splits.
c4: an unquoted RHS of contains/startsWith/endsWith resolves through the variable map; a quoted RHS stays a literal.
c5: == and != are numeric when both sides parse as numbers ('5.0' == 5); string equality, ordering operators and booleans are unchanged; missing == null.
c6: an unrecognized multi-word condition throws; a single variable name, including a key that contains a space, keeps its truthiness behavior.

m1: look for collateral behavior changes, such as lowercase and/or splitting text that used to be literal, new errors in conditions that were valid before, and numeric equality applied to quoted string literals.
Look for evidence that the full pre-existing suite passes after the change.

findings.title: No evidence that the pre-existing test suite still passes; the new error path and lowercase and/or splitting could change previously valid conditions

serves.scenario: The goal-critical question 'do all pre-existing tests still pass?' cannot be answered from the packet. The diff makes three changes that can break earlier behavior. (1) Any condition with bare whitespace that matches no operator now throws, even in lenient mode. Before, a condition such as `a + b` or two words evaluated to false. (2) Lowercase `and`/`or` between words now split conditions. (3) The string-operator RHS now goes through resolveValue. If resolveValue does not strip single quotes the way the removed regex did (/^["']|["']$/), then `s startsWith 'hello'` would become a variable lookup and return false. If any existing test relies on one of these behaviors, it now fails.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope; goal-critical: do all pre-existing tests still pass?
findings.reproduction: Run the full jest suite at head 413e6517 and compare it with base e7069db. Separately, at head, resolve `{{IF a + b}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}}` with a=1, b=2 in lenient mode. It throws 'Unrecognized condition' where base rendered N. Also confirm that resolveValue("'hello'") returns the literal hello.
evidence: test:guard-existing-forms: NOT(a), AND, OR and quoted contains keep working

findings.title: Numeric equality now also applies to quoted string literals and non-decimal numeric strings

serves.scenario: valuesEqual coerces any string that tryCoerceToNumber accepts. So `zip == "01234"` with zip = "1234" is now true. If tryCoerceToNumber is Number-based, '0x10' == '16' and '1e3' == '1000' are also true. These still meet the letter of c5 ('both sides numeric'), but a quoted literal written as a string now compares as a number. The lead may want that scope stated explicitly.

findings.rubric: no change outside the card scope
findings.reproduction: At head, render `{{IF z == "01234"}}Y{{ELSE}}N{{END_IF}}` with z = "1234". It gives Y, where base gave N.

findings.title: The unknown-word error fires on any unmatched multi-word condition, not only on a word next to an operator

serves.scenario: hasBareWhitespace throws for any condition that contains bare whitespace and matched no operator, for example `a b` or `a + b`. That is broader than 'an unknown word next to an operator'. It is probably the intended direction, but it widens the error surface beyond what the criterion says.
